notes:
Account summary: Lakota is an algorithmic market analysis platform (equities/derivatives) building a latency-sensitive trading assistant and real-time reranker. They are procurement-stage for Dedicated capacity; security and legal are heavily involved.

Recent wins/ask: committed to 8x H100-equivalent GPUs initially, want explicit guarantee that H100 capacity is available for the term or automatic compatible fallback. Requesting throughput/latency SLOs written into the contract. Cost-sensitive but prioritize availability for trading hours.

SLA negotiation highlights:
- Lakota legal pushing for 99.99% monthly uptime. Redwood standard Dedicated draft: 99.95% with credit schedule. Legal counters: higher credits and faster remediation commitments.
- Redwood proposed credit tiers (internal draft shared in 2026-02-25 call): 10% credit if uptime 99.9-99.95, 25% for 99.5-99.9, 50% <99.5. Lakota marked these as low for their risk profile; counter ask: larger credits and pro-rated per-hour calculations for major incidents.
- Maintenance windows: Redwood proposes bi-weekly 60-minute maintenance windows, scheduled 02:00-05:00 UTC. Lakota wants maintenance blackout for 14:30-22:30 US/Eastern (their market open/close) and expressed need for at most one planned maintenance per month during off-hours.
- Support and escalation: Lakota requires P1 response <= 15 minutes (phone + dedicated Slack channel), P2 <= 1 hour, P3 <= 4 hours. Redwood can offer 24/7 on-call for P1/P2 under enterprise SLA (add-on).
- Throughput/latency SLOs: target p95 inference latency < 120ms for 1k-token chat/rerank requests; baseline throughput: 20 concurrent requests sustained, burst to 50 for 10 minutes. Asked for guardrails: queueing limits, circuit-breaker behavior, and guaranteed reserved batch slots.
- Reserved GPU planning: committed 8x H100 (or equivalent). Discussed warm pool strategy (keep 10% spare capacity for burst), pre-warming KV caches for predictable seq-lengths, startup provisioning time to scale reserved pods (target < 5 minutes for warmup).
- Fallback routing: must have automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant for non-critical traffic; trading queries must never fall back without explicit route rule (i.e., fail closed for primary model for trading-critical path).
- Data controls: KMS-managed keys, audit logs exported to their SIEM, weekly retention snapshots for debug (30 days), data residency: primary region us-east-1.
